Why this matters for SSC

Boundary line questions (Radcliffe, McMahon, Durand, etc.) come every year — typically 1–2 marks. The trick: remember the line and what it separates.

---

India's land borders — overview

India shares land borders with 7 countries:

CountryLength (approx)Indian states on the border
Bangladesh4,096 km (longest)West Bengal, Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram
China3,488 kmLadakh, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Sikkim, Arunachal Pradesh
Pakistan3,323 kmJ&K, Ladakh, Punjab, Rajasthan, Gujarat
Nepal1,770 kmUttarakhand, UP, Bihar, West Bengal, Sikkim
Myanmar1,643 kmArunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram
Bhutan659 kmSikkim, West Bengal, Assam, Arunachal Pradesh
Afghanistan106 km (via PoK — Wakhan Corridor)Ladakh (PoK)

Total land border: ~15,200 km.

Coastline (incl. islands): ~7,516 km; Mainland: ~5,422 km; Andaman & Nicobar + Lakshadweep: ~2,094 km.

---

Internal boundaries (between Indian states)

LineSeparates
Radcliffe LineIndia and Pakistan (1947) — drawn by Sir Cyril Radcliffe; total length 3,323 km.
Radcliffe Line (East)India and East Pakistan (now Bangladesh) — drawn by Radcliffe; ~4,096 km
McMahon LineIndia (Arunachal Pradesh) and China (Tibet) — 1914, drawn by Sir Arthur Henry McMahon at the Simla Convention. Length ~890 km. China disputes it; it is the de facto boundary.
Durand LineAfghanistan and Pakistan — 1893, drawn by Sir Mortimer Durand; not an India–Afghanistan border, but India inherited the PoK border with Afghanistan (Wakhan corridor).
Line of Control (LoC)India and Pakistan in J&K and Ladakh — established after the 1971 war; 740 km long.
Line of Actual Control (LAC)India and China — de facto border, not officially demarcated. ~3,488 km. Divided into 3 sectors: Western (Ladakh), Middle (Uttarakhand/HP), Eastern (Sikkim/Arunachal).
Sir CreekDisputed estuary between India (Gujarat — Kutch) and Pakistan (Sindh). ~96 km.
17th ParallelIndia (Manipur/Mizoram side) and Myanmar — proposed demarcation, also known as Pemberton Line (proposed by Robert Boileau Pemberton, 1830s) — note: Pemberton Line is the older British name; commonly referred to as the 17th Parallel today.
22nd ParallelMentioned in the India–Pakistan context (Rann of Kutch).
24th ParallelDemarcation in the western sector (Sir Creek debate) — sometimes confused with 24th parallel is the proposed boundary.
Attari–Wagah BorderIndia–Pakistan border near Amritsar (Punjab) — famous for the Beating Retreat ceremony.
Zero LineIndia–Nepal border; 1,770 km; open border, no restrictions.
Nathu LaIndia–China border in Sikkim — open since 2006 for trade.
Jogbani–BiratnagarIndia–Nepal border, Bihar side.
Varanasi–RaxaulBihar side, India–Nepal.
Petrapole–BenapoleIndia–Bangladesh border (West Bengal) — major land customs.
HiliIndia–Bangladesh border (West Bengal).

Historical Boundary Lines

LinePurpose / YearDrawn byKey facts
Radcliffe LineIndia–Pakistan (1947) and India–Bangladesh (1947)Sir Cyril RadcliffeBoundary of 1947 Partition of India; 5,000+ km.
McMahon LineIndia–China (Tibet) (1914)Sir Henry McMahonSimla Convention 1914; China does not recognise it.
Durand LineAfghanistan–Pakistan (1893)Sir Mortimer DurandAfghanistan has never officially recognised it.
Hindu LineIndia–Pakistan in Rajasthan (1965)Indian forces, 1965 Indo-Pak warCreated by Indian Army under Major General Sukhwant Singh during the 1965 war. Drawn up to 8 km inside Pakistani territory.
Hemis LineIndia–Tibet (China)19th century British / TibetTawang sector.
Pemberton LineIndia–Myanmar (1830s)Robert Boileau PembertonOlder demarcation.
Lansdowne LineIndia–AfghanistanBritish India, 19th centuryNorthern frontier of British India.
Johnson LineIndia–China (Ladakh–Aksai Chin)Sir George Johnson (1865)Shows Aksai Chin as part of India; the Johnson Line is not the present border, but is the line for which India historically claimed Aksai Chin.
Gansser LineAksai Chin (geological)Augusto Gansser (Swiss geologist)Not a political line; named for geology.
Blue LineIsrael–Lebanon–Golan Heights (UN-demarcated)UNNot relevant to India, but often confused in SSC.
Green LineUN buffer zone in CyprusUNNot relevant to India.
Line of Control (LoC)India–Pakistan (J&K and Ladakh)UN observers after 1971 war740 km; frozen conflict; ceasefire line.
Line of Actual Control (LAC)India–China (de facto)—3,488 km; not demarcated; buffer zones.
Working BoundaryIndia–Pakistan (Sindh–Rajasthan sector)—Opposite term for LoC/AGL.
Mannerheim LineRussia–Finland (WWII)Baron Carl Gustaf Emil MannerheimNot India-related.

---

Quick recall for exam

  • Radcliffe Line = India–Pakistan (and India–Bangladesh), Cyril Radcliffe, 1947.
  • McMahon Line = India–China, McMahon, 1914 Simla Convention.
  • Durand Line = Afghanistan–Pakistan, 1893.
  • LoC = India–Pakistan, 1971 war ceasefire, J&K+Ladakh, 740 km.
  • LAC = India–China, de facto, 3,488 km, 3 sectors.
  • Hindu Line = India drew inside Pak in 1965 — Sukhwant Singh.
  • 17th Parallel = India–Myanmar (older Pemberton Line).
  • Johnson Line = India–China (Aksai Chin claim basis).
  • Attari–Wagah = India–Pakistan in Punjab — beating retreat.
  • Sir Creek = India–Pakistan, Gujarat–Sindh.
  • Indira Point = Southernmost of India (Andaman).
  • Indira Col = Northernmost of India (Ladakh).
  • Kanyakumari = Southernmost of mainland.

Key concepts

  • 7 land neighbours (incl. Afghanistan via PoK).
  • Radcliffe Line: 1947, Cyril Radcliffe.
  • McMahon Line: 1914, McMahon; China does not recognise.
  • Durand Line: 1893, Mortimer Durand.
  • LAC vs LoC: de facto vs ceasefire.
  • 17th parallel = India–Myanmar; Pemberton Line is the older name.
  • 38th parallel = North–South Korea; 17th parallel = North–South Vietnam.

2024–2025 Updates

  • India-Bangladesh enclaves: All 162 enclaves were exchanged in 2015; this remains settled. By 2024–25, the relationship includes cooperation on smuggling, border fencing, and Teesta water-sharing (still under negotiation).
  • India-Myanmar: Free Movement Regime (FMR) was partly modified in 2024–25 in light of ethnic conflict in Manipur; FMR continues but with tightened documentation.
  • India-China LAC: Dis-engagement talks continued in 2024–25; status of Depsang and Demchok regions remain in focus. No change in LAC length (~3,488 km).
  • India-Maldives: After 2023 diplomatic row, relations stabilised in 2024 with India continuing to be the "first responder" for the Maldives.
  • Sir Creek: India-Pakistan talks (technical-level) continued in 2024–25; no resolution.
  • Attari-Wagah border: Beating Retreat ceremony continues daily; in 2024–25 the joint parade for India's Republic Day (26 Jan) and Pakistan's National Day (23 Mar) resumed.
  • India-Nepal border: 1,770 km, open border, continues. India also facilitated the construction of ₹1,600 crore-worth cross-border bridges in 2024.
No new boundary lines were added in 2024–25. The 7 land neighbours remain the same: Pakistan, China, Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh, Myanmar, Afghanistan (via PoK).
